planting.note: Set out nursery starts once frost danger has passed into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; this dwarf selection is especially unforgiving of soggy winter clay, so a raised bed or slope helps it persist on the Gulf Coast.

directions: Purple Pygmy is a naturally compact selection of the Texas native Agastache cana, growing barely over a foot tall yet still producing the species' signature wands of vivid purplish-pink, bubblegum-scented flowers from midsummer into fall. Its tidy, dense habit makes it useful in smaller beds, raised planters, and rock gardens where full-size cana selections would sprawl. Plant it in lean, fast-draining soil in full sun; once established it shrugs off heat and drought and needs water only during prolonged dry spells. Hummingbirds and bees visit constantly through the long bloom season, and the aromatic foliage stays deer- and rabbit-resistant throughout.

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring in lean, average to sandy, sharply drained soil in full sun; good winter drainage matters more than extreme cold hardiness for this selection.

directions: Cherry Queen is a long-cultivated autumn sage selection prized for flowers of a clear, saturated cherry red, brighter than most straight Salvia greggii forms, a trait traced to its partial S. blepharophylla parentage. It forms a rounded, woody-based subshrub roughly knee to waist height that blooms in flushes from late spring through the first hard frost. Give it full sun and lean, sharply drained soil; established plants tolerate Gulf Coast heat and drought well but benefit from a hard cutback in late winter to renew dense, floriferous growth. Hummingbirds visit the tubular flowers steadily, and the plant holds up reliably through zone 8-9 winters given good drainage.
